files.lesson.md: --- order: 11 unit: sci9 node: AC9M9M02 n2 uses: [AC9M9M02 n1, AC9M9A01 n2] assumes: [AC9M8N02 n1, AC9M8N02 n2, AC9M9A01 n1, AC9M9A01 n2] connection: sunlight-time title: Calculating in scientific notation summary: "Multiply or divide the number parts, add or subtract the powers of 10, then check the number part is still from 1 to 10." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Light takes about 8 minutes to reach us from the Sun. How far is that, without a calculator?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8348 url: http://127.0.0.1:8348/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: calc.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$15 \\times 10^{10}$ is $1.5 \\times 10^{11}$: the number part has to be from 1 to 10, so move a factor of 10 into the power." } explainClip: query: { code: "@calc.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Fix the number part, then fix the power" say: "Fifteen times ten to the ten has a number part that's too big." clip: - caption: { text: "15 × 10¹⁰: the number part is too big.", say: "Fifteen is too big for the number part." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "15 = 1.5 × 10, so one more 10 goes in the power.", say: "Fifteen is one point five times ten. That adds one to the power." } - click: Make k bigger - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "1.5 × 10¹¹.", say: "One point five times ten to the eleven." } - wait: 800 --- Scientific notation is made for calculating. The number parts multiply and the powers of 10 follow the index laws. ## Predict: the distance to the Sun ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a distance shows who slips by a power of 10 when multiplying a speed and a time." check: type: predict q: "Light travels at $3 \\times 10^{8}$ m/s. It takes about 500 seconds ($5 \\times 10^{2}$) to reach us from the Sun. How far is the Sun?" options: - "$1.5 \\times 10^{11}$ m" - "$1.5 \\times 10^{10}$ m" - "$1.5 \\times 10^{12}$ m" - "$8 \\times 10^{10}$ m" actual: "1.5 × 10¹¹ m. Distance = speed × time = (3 × 10⁸) × (5 × 10²) = 15 × 10¹⁰ = 1.5 × 10¹¹ m: 150 million kilometres." ``` Sunlight takes about 500 seconds. How far has it come? Don't use a calculator. ## Run: fix the number part ```step stage: run insight: "Multiplying the number parts can give 10 or more. Then the number part is rewritten from 1 to 10, and the power changes to match." try: { playground: board, starter: "calc.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "$3 \\times 5 = 15$ and $10^{8} \\times 10^{2} = 10^{10}$, so the answer is $15 \\times 10^{10}$. Set the board to the same number with a number part from 1 to 10. Was your prediction right?", when: "a = 1.5 and k = 11" } ``` The board writes $a \times 10^k$ out. Which values of $a$ and $k$ give the same number as $15 \times 10^{10}$? ## Investigate: number parts, then powers ```step stage: investigate insight: "Multiply the number parts, add the powers, then fix the number part if it's 10 or more. Mia stops one step early." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Work out $(2 \\times 10^{3}) \\times (3 \\times 10^{4})$ as $6 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: 7 explain: "2 × 3 = 6 and 3 + 4 = 7: 6 × 10⁷." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia works out $(4 \\times 10^{3}) \\times (5 \\times 10^{4})$. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: sci-not-normalised explain: "Line 4: 20 × 10⁷ isn't in scientific notation, because 20 is more than 10. 20 = 2 × 10, so it's 2 × 10⁸." - check: type: question q: "What is $(6 \\times 10^{5}) \\div (2 \\times 10^{2})$?" options: ["$3 \\times 10^{3}$", "$3 \\times 10^{7}$", "$4 \\times 10^{3}$", "$3 \\times 10^{2.5}$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Divide means subtract the powers: 5 − 2 = 3.", "Divide the number parts: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.", "Subtract the whole powers: 5 − 2."] explain: "6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 10⁵ ÷ 10² = 10³." ``` ### Multiply Here's the whole routine, with a number part that grows. ```worked (3 \times 10^{8}) \times (5 \times 10^{2}) :: Speed times time. 3 \times 5 = 15 :: Multiply the number parts. 10^{8} \times 10^{2} = 10^{10} :: Add the powers. 15 \times 10^{10} :: Too big: the number part is 10 or more. 1.5 \times 10 \times 10^{10} :: 15 = 1.5 × 10. 1.5 \times 10^{11} :: Add the extra 10 to the power. ``` Now try one on paper: $(2.5 \times 10^{4}) \times (4 \times 10^{3})$. Then type the power in your answer. ### Find the mistake Read Mia's working. Is 20 allowed as the number part? ### Divide ## Modify: change the calculation ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: division, a negative power, then adding instead of multiplying." try: { playground: board, starter: "calc.yml#vary", height: 620 } tasks: - hint: ["Divide the number parts: 8 ÷ 2.", "Subtract the powers: 7 − 4."] check: { type: number, q: "Work out $(8 \\times 10^{7}) \\div (2 \\times 10^{4})$ as $4 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?", answer: 3, explain: "8 ÷ 2 = 4 and 7 − 4 = 3: 4 × 10³." } - hint: ["Add the powers: −3 + 5.", "Multiply the number parts: 3 × 2."] check: { type: number, q: "Work out $(3 \\times 10^{-3}) \\times (2 \\times 10^{5})$ as $6 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?", answer: 2, explain: "3 × 2 = 6 and −3 + 5 = 2: 6 × 10²." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the powers: what's $-3 + 5$?", answer: 2, explain: "−3 + 5 = 2." } - hint: ["You can't add the powers: these are added numbers.", "Write both as ordinary numbers first."] check: { type: answer, q: "Edge case: work out $3 \\times 10^{4} + 2 \\times 10^{3}$ as an ordinary number.", answer: "32000", form: simplified, feedback: [["5 × 10^7", "Adding doesn't add the powers. 30 000 + 2 000."], ["50000", "3 × 10⁴ = 30 000 and 2 × 10³ = 2 000."]], explain: "30 000 + 2 000 = 32 000, or 3.2 × 10⁴." } ``` ### Divide ### Negative power ### Add ## Practise: calculate ```step stage: practise insight: "Multiplying, dividing and fixing the number part, mixed; the review keeps conversion fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Work out $(2 \\times 10^{5}) \\times (3 \\times 10^{2})$ as $6 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: 7 explain: "2 × 3 = 6 and 5 + 2 = 7." - check: type: number q: "Work out $(9 \\times 10^{6}) \\times (6 \\times 10^{3})$ as $5.4 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: 10 explain: "9 × 6 = 54 and 6 + 3 = 9: 54 × 10⁹ = 5.4 × 10¹⁰." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just 9 × 6: what's the number part before it's fixed?", answer: 54, explain: "9 × 6 = 54. Then 54 = 5.4 × 10, which adds 1 to the power." } - check: type: number q: "Work out $(6 \\times 10^{-2}) \\div (3 \\times 10^{4})$ as $2 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: -6 explain: "6 ÷ 3 = 2 and −2 − 4 = −6." - check: type: number q: "Review: write $0.0063$ as $6.3 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: -3 explain: "The point moves 3 places right: k = −3." ``` ### Multiply ### A bigger number part ### Divide ### Review Conversion, from the last lesson. ## Make: back to the Sun ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the opening: the whole routine on a real distance, then a check against a published value." tasks: - hint: ["Distance = speed × time.", "Multiply the number parts, add the powers, fix the number part."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Light travels at $3 \\times 10^{8}$ m/s and takes about 500 s to reach us from the Sun. Work out the distance in metres in scientific notation. What's the power of 10?" steps: - ["$500 = 5 \\times 10^{2}$", "write the time in scientific notation"] - ["$(3 \\times 10^{8}) \\times (5 \\times 10^{2}) = 15 \\times 10^{10}$", "multiply the number parts, add the powers"] - ["$15 \\times 10^{10} = 1.5 \\times 10^{11}$", "fix the number part"] answer: "11" answerLabel: "The power of 10" feedback: - ["10", "15 × 10¹⁰ still needs fixing: the number part is more than 10."] - ["12", "15 = 1.5 × 10, so add 1 to 10, not 2."] criteria: - "I wrote 500 as 5 × 10²." - "My number part is from 1 to 10." - "My answer matches 1.5 × 10¹¹ m." explain: "1.5 × 10¹¹ m." - check: type: number q: "NASA gives the average distance as 150 million km. In metres, that's $1.5 \\times 10^{k}$. What's $k$?" answer: 11 explain: "150 million km = 150 000 000 000 m = 1.5 × 10¹¹ m. It matches." ``` ### The distance Back to the Sun. Work it out on paper first, then type the power. ### Check with NASA Light time: [Smithsonian](https://howthingsfly.si.edu/ask-an-explainer/how-long-does-it-take-light-sun-get-earth) says about 8 minutes 20 seconds, which is about 500 s. Speed of light: [NIST](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/Value/c.html). Earth's average distance from the Sun: [NASA](https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/). Earth's orbit isn't a perfect circle, so the distance changes a little through the year. **Also used in** - **Computing.** Data sizes and speeds are multiplied and divided in powers of 10. - **Next lesson.** Using scientific notation for real measurements, from medicine to space. ```teacher summary: Students multiply and divide numbers in scientific notation using the index laws, fix the number part when it reaches 10 or more, and use the speed of light and a time to find the distance to the Sun (AC9M9M02, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can multiply and divide numbers in scientific notation. - I can fix the number part so it's from 1 to 10. - I can use scientific notation to find a distance from a speed and a time. struggle: "Remembering the last step: check the number part. Ask students to circle it before they write the answer." before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Scientific notation and All the index laws. The one idea: multiply or divide the number parts, add or subtract the powers, then fix the number part. The common mistake is stopping at 20 × 10⁷ (Mia's working). Figures: light time about 8 minutes 20 seconds (Smithsonian), speed of light exact (NIST), distance 150 million km (NASA). The lesson uses 500 s. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose 1.5 × 10¹⁰ lost the extra power from fixing 15." - "Run: ask students to say what 15 × 10¹⁰ is in words before changing the board." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the Sun distance in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for the step that fixes the number part." - "Modify: before 3 × 10⁴ + 2 × 10³, ask whether you can add the powers." stuck: - see: A student stops at 20 × 10⁷. ask: Is 20 between 1 and 10? fix: "No: 20 = 2 × 10, so 2 × 10⁸." - see: A student adds numbers by adding powers. ask: What's 30 000 + 2 000? fix: "Write them as ordinary numbers: the index laws are for multiplying and dividing." stretch: Light from the Moon takes about 1.3 seconds. How far is the Moon? Check it. support: "A flow card: multiply number parts, add powers, check the number part." leads: | Continues AC9M9M02 node 2. Where it leads: measurements in science and medicine (next). exit: q: Work out (4 × 10⁶) × (5 × 10⁻²) in scientific notation. a: 2 × 10⁵. explain: > To multiply, multiply the number parts and add the powers. To divide, divide the number parts and subtract the powers. Then check the number part is from 1 to 10: if it's 10 or more, move a factor of 10 into the power. $(3 \times 10^8) \times (5 \times 10^2) = 15 \times 10^{10} = 1.5 \times 10^{11}$. ```

# region: mia
Work out (4 × 10³) × (5 × 10⁴).
Multiply the numbers: 4 × 5 = 20.
Add the powers: 3 + 4 = 7.
So the answer is 20 × 10⁷.
